summary: ESCALATION of the 04:21Z signal (same dedup_key, do not double-mint): the hot/cold next_agent divergence does not merely skip individual rows — it empties the Review-Lane QA-Drain candidate set entirely. Measured live this tick.

payload.why_escalated: Previously filed as 2 individual mis-resolved rows. A full census this tick shows the lane-level consequence: QA-Drain resolves ZERO eligible rows out of 27 review[] rows while holding 7 free budget (QA_WIP=3, QA_CAP=10). The lane is dammed, not merely lossy.

masking_row.note: This is the ONLY review[] row routed to qa on the hot board. effective_next_agent() prefers the cold backlog-detail.json value, so it resolves to developer and QA-Drain never sees it. One stale cold entry is sufficient to zero the entire lane.

payload.reproduce: jq -r --slurpfile detail docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json (build id-keyed map from .items[]) then compare .task_board.review[].next_agent against $D[.id].next_agent; count rows where the cold value wins and differs.
payload.root_cause_location: scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq:342-348 effective_next_agent($detail_items) returns $detail_items[.id].next_agent whenever it is a non-empty string, falling back to the hot row .next_agent only when absent. detail_items_from (:49-53) builds that map from docs/data/orch/archive/backlog-detail.json .items[]. Nothing reconciles the two planes and nothing warns on mismatch.
asks: Decide which plane is authoritative for next_agent. The hot board is the one every agent actually writes on handoff; the cold archive is a snapshot that goes stale silently.

Until that decision lands, make the divergence loud rather than silent: have effective_next_agent (or a preflight audit) emit a warning listing rows where hot and cold disagree, instead of resolving one and discarding the other.
Re-check the QA-Drain lane after the fix. Its DoD trend (review[] shrinks, qa[] grows) cannot be measured while its candidate set resolves to zero.
